name: KM3NeT/ORCA — Toulon deep-sea site
notes: ANTARES (site:antares-toulon, detector:antares) sits about 10 km east of this site per the Letter of Intent ('ORCA ... approximately 10 kilometers west of the existing ANTARES telescope site'), but site:antares-toulon belongs to no Atlas facility (its facility_id is null), so it is outside this map's inventory: it is not drawn and not listed as not drawn. Its own coordinate is only 'approximate' with precision_m 12000 (a corroborated estimate, not a directly published lat/lon), which is too coarse to add a defensibly placed context point here anyway.

The ORCA shore control station has moved between buildings (Institut Michel Pacha, La Seyne-sur-Mer originally; the Brégaillon/Ifremer site since January 2024; the MEUST building once ready), so no single building was confidently identified as the shore station to draw as OpenStreetMap context; it is not drawn.
OpenStreetMap was not used for the two drawn features: a sea site has no OSM footprint.

summary.plain: The Mediterranean seabed site off Toulon, France, where the KM3NeT/ORCA neutrino telescope is being built, about 40 km offshore and 2450 m down.
summary.technical: Local map for the KM3NeT-Fr / ORCA deep-sea site (facility:km3net). One surveyed point (the collaboration's own published 42°48' N 06°02' E) and one derived ~200 m-diameter circle for the single ORCA building block, its radius estimated by scaling ARCA's sourced R=500 m by the two blocks' relative string spacing (both from the KM3NeT 2.0 Letter of Intent). ARCA and ORCA are ~900 km apart and cannot share a to-scale map; see map:km3net-arca (linked).
